target.title: fix(telegram): bound stalled diagnostic response reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Telegram diagnostics and membership audits could keep waiting after the Bot API returned response headers but then stalled or only trickled the response body.

## Why This Change Was Made

Telegram Bot API diagnostic body reads now use a Telegram-local bounded reader with the existing byte cap, a per-chunk idle timeout, and an overall body deadline. The change covers `getMe`, best-effort `getWebhookInfo`, and membership-audit `getChatMember` reads without changing fetch/header timeout or webhook best-effort semantics.

## User Impact

Telegram setup checks and membership audits now fail or degrade on a bounded deadline instead of appearing to spin forever on a stuck response body.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/response-body-timeout.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/probe.response-body-timeout.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/probe.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/audit.test.ts` (22 tests passed)
- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD`
- Claude autoreview: clean, no accepted/actionable findings
### Exact-head controlled-network proof

Exact head: `f174acb7b443a366fed7048448884d226dab886f`.

Command:

```text
HTTP_PROXY= HTTPS_PROXY= http_proxy= https_proxy= ALL_PROXY= all_proxy= NO_PROXY=127.0.0.1,localhost no_proxy=127.0.0.1,localhost node_modules/.bin/tsx scratchpad/telegram-diagnostic-exact-head-proof.mts
```

The temporary harness was removed after the run. It called production `probeTelegram()` and `auditTelegramGroupMembership()` through the production Telegram undici transport, routing only the Bot API root to a loopback `node:http` server. It used a redacted fake token, no mocked adapter, no real Telegram traffic, and no credentials.

Redacted transcript:

```text
proof: exact-head production Telegram diagnostics against local Bot API
exact-head: f174acb7b443a366fed7048448884d226dab886f
apiRoot: http://127.0.0.1:<redacted-port>
server: accepted getMe mode=header-stall
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 295ms (elapsed 296ms) operation=fetchWithTimeout url=http://127.0.0.1:<redacted-port>/bot***/getMe
probe: mode=header-stall ok=false error=request timed out webhook=none elapsed=360ms
server: client closed getMe
server: accepted getMe mode=body-stall
probe: mode=body-stall ok=false error=Telegram diagnostic response body stalled for 139ms webhook=none elapsed=168ms
server: client closed getMe
server: accepted getMe mode=trickle
probe: mode=trickle ok=false error=Telegram diagnostic response body timed out after 295ms webhook=none elapsed=302ms
server: client closed getMe
server: accepted getMe mode=normal
probe: mode=normal ok=true error=none webhook=none elapsed=6ms
server: accepted getMe mode=webhook-body-stall
server: accepted getWebhookInfo mode=webhook-body-stall
probe: mode=webhook-body-stall ok=true error=none webhook=none elapsed=156ms
server: client closed getWebhookInfo
server: accepted getChatMember mode=audit-body-stall
audit: mode=audit-body-stall ok=false error=Telegram membership audit response body stalled for 150ms elapsed=179ms
server: client closed getChatMember
server: accepted getChatMember mode=audit-normal
audit: mode=audit-normal ok=true status=member elapsed=6ms
server: aborted-response-count=5
```

Observed: header, partial-body, and slow-trickle failures return within the harness budget and close their sockets; a later normal diagnostic succeeds; webhook body failure remains best-effort; membership audit fails boundedly and then recovers on a normal response. All assertions passed; exit 0.

Known limits: this is controlled local Bot API transport proof, not live Telegram. The 300 ms caller budget is for the proof harness and is not the production default. The exact command referenced a temporary uncommitted harness that has been removed.


### Current-head CI follow-up

Current merge head after the ordinary GitHub `update-branch`: `60fa08969d9b011d0996572770d4992eeea4d0ff`. Contributor fix commit: `dd69ccd53f046e6ee6472fe5576b48a15646fd87`.

Secretless GitHub CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29244735197

- `check-test-types`: passed; the earlier TS2493 in `extensions/telegram/src/response-body-timeout.test.ts` is fixed by typing the cancellation mock's optional reason argument.
- `check-prod-types`, `check-additional-extension-bundled`, `checks-node-compact-small-2`, and all Node test shards: passed.
- 59 checks passed overall; no checks remain pending.
- `check-lint` still fails only in `src/gateway/server-lanes.ts` and `src/agents/session-suspension.ts`, both inherited from the merged `main` snapshot and outside this PR's Telegram diff.
- `check-dependencies` still fails on the inherited stale dead-export baseline entry `src/config/sessions/types.ts: QuotaSuspension`, outside this PR's Telegram diff.

Known limits: the controlled local Bot API proof above was run at `f174acb7b443a366fed7048448884d226dab886f` and is not presented as a live Telegram run or as rerun at this merge head. The contributor follow-up changes only test mock typing; no credentialed local/Testbox execution was used.
